status: Developer inventory draft, not a completed or submitted Play Data Safety declaration.
scope: Source inventory of the existing backend/web capabilities and the current native source candidate, including native owned booking history and explicit read-only rate review. These new native flows are not claimed to be present in an earlier delivered APK. SDK collection, permissions and final declaration answers must be verified against the Android build actually released.

source_baseline.backend_evidence: Immutable Git source at this commit, especially services/userAuthRoutes.js. The older backend files inherited by the mobile worktree are not the authority for these API contracts.
source_baseline.native_evidence: Current apps/mobile source candidate; source paths below describe implementation, not a completed Play declaration or device-runtime verification.
source_baseline.interpretation_limit: Receiving or discarding a response field is recorded as a source fact here. This inventory does not decide Play collection/sharing exceptions, legal purposes, required/optional declarations, retention periods or compliance.

observed_data: Password input sent to the backend over HTTPS for login/registration
Password hash stored and compared on the server
Session token hash, role, realm and expiry on the server
data_flows.native_implementation: The client receives an opaque 64-hex-character access_token, uses Authorization: Bearer for authenticated API requests and never adds that token to a URL. Native token persistence uses Expo SecureStore; the web preview uses memory only. Session profile state is held in memory. These storage facts are not an account-retention or deletion policy.
data_flows.deletion_gap: No account-deletion request handler or associated-data workflow found in the audited baseline; logout is session termination, not account deletion.

data_flows.flow: Native owned booking history and accompanying profile response
request_data: Existing account bearer session token in the Authorization header
data_flows.ownership_observed: The backend requires a user session, resolves the profile with the authenticated subject and email, and queries bookings by authenticated ownerSubject plus realm. The native helper sends no email, owner identifier or other identity query parameter.
data_flows.processing_observed: The complete JSON response reaches native transport parsing before normalization. This therefore introduces native receipt/processing of account name, email, optional phone, loyalty points, saved-card holder/masked-number metadata, traveler/customer name and booking/payment metadata even though the history view discards most of it. This route does not return a password hash, full card number, CVC or card payment token in its public serializers; masked-card metadata is still received.
history_model_retains_in_memory: Raw record and supplier status text with a derived presentation category
Explicit customer price and priceCurrency only for known persisted providers
data_flows.local_handling_observed: History results are kept in React memory without a disk/browser-storage cache. The rendered result is keyed by authentication status, monotonically changing session revision and refresh attempt, so a previous session's rows are hidden immediately on an identity/revision change. Outstanding requests are aborted; late aborted results are rejected. This describes display isolation and non-persistence, not guaranteed immediate memory erasure or backend deletion.
data_flows.actions_observed: Display, refresh/retry and sign-in navigation only. The history screen creates no booking, payment, cancellation, refund or voucher request.
data_flows.purpose_in_code: Display the signed-in account's existing booking records.

services/userAuthRoutes.js:193-217 (owned profile route at the authoritative backend commit)
data_flows.declaration_gate: Review the actual transferred profile/contact, saved-card metadata and booking/payment fields when preparing the final declaration. Client-side discarding does not mean those fields never reached the app. No new retention/deletion guarantee or completed Play answer is asserted.

data_flows.flow: Native selected-offer review, explicit read-only prebook and RAM-only draft
request_data: Requested currency and language for hotel/search reads
Original h-prefixed offer hash and signed offer_context for an explicit prebook price check
Existing bearer session token in the Authorization header when signed in
response_data: Tax amounts, currencies and inclusion flags
Returned p-prefixed hash and signed prebook_context, validated transiently by the client
local_draft_data: Selected hotel identifier/name and optional address/image
Original selected offer including signed offer_context, room identity, price, taxes and cancellation terms
Local draft identifier and creation time
Local owner key derived from app environment, authentication status and session revision
In-memory recheck status, updated offer terms, change acceptance and expiry
data_flows.local_handling_observed: The draft and recheck state live only in JavaScript/React memory. They are not written to AsyncStorage, SecureStore, browser storage, logs or deep links by the review implementation. The draft is bound to the current environment/authentication revision and search criteria, becomes inaccessible on identity/search changes and is cleared by the corresponding state handlers. Selection validity is five minutes and displayed recheck validity is at most two minutes within that selection window; these are UI validity limits, not deletion/retention guarantees. The returned prebook_context is validated in the API result and is not persisted or used to create a payment/booking by this review flow.
data_flows.actions_observed: The user explicitly requests a price/terms recheck of the original signed h-offer. A returned p-offer is not reused as a new recheck input. Changed terms require acceptance before a fixed HTTPS website handoff. The handoff carries hotel/search criteria only; it carries no bearer session token, offer/prebook capability, traveler contact or payment information and requires website reselection/recheck. No native quote, payment-intent, supplier booking form/finish, cancellation or refund endpoint is called by this feature.
data_flows.purpose_in_code: Let the user inspect the selected offer and current price/tax/cancellation terms before continuing on the website.
source_files: server.js (/api/search/hotelpage and /api/booking/prebook at the authoritative backend commit)
data_flows.declaration_gate: Assess search/occupancy data, account linkage, supplier transfers and any website handoff in the final shipped flow. Memory-only handling and a read-only price check do not establish a Play exemption or a legal retention/deletion conclusion.

data_flows.flow: Hotel search, selection, guests and reservation servicing
data_flows.recipient_questions: Confirm the exact fields sent to each accommodation supplier. Supplier confirmation email is configured separately; do not assume the customer's email is sent to every provider.
data_flows.retention_gate: Approve and disclose reservation/accounting retention and deletion handling; do not promise that all historical financial records are immediately erased.

observed_data: Passport identity-page image or Emirates ID front/back images
Review status, notes and audit events
data_flows.storage_observed: Documents are encrypted and access-scoped. Draft upload expiry is 24 hours; submission/review changes expiry, with final decision retention capped at 30 days in the inspected implementation. Application/review metadata is a separate retained record.
release_gates: Verify the actual cleanup/TTL behavior operationally; a schema expiry is not evidence every record has been removed.
Explain document collection and retention clearly before upload.
Confirm final Play data categories, required/optional status, processors and any OCR SDK/provider behavior.
Never include real identity documents in store screenshots, fixtures or reviewer instructions.

data_flows.provider_gate: Audit the final hosted-payment/native SDK flow. Do not declare Remal card-number/CVC collection merely because a payment gateway handles cards, or declare no collection without checking the shipped integration.
data_flows.retention_gate: Payment and booking references may have legitimate retention requirements; the actual policy and associated-data deletion process remain to be approved.

observed_data: Booking user IP supplied to supplier booking-form creation
data_flows.classification_gate: Inspect final logging, retention and purposes. Hotel coordinates or a searched destination do not by themselves prove device GPS/location collection. Do not request or declare location access without the actual feature/permission inventory.

observed_data: Hotel name/location/place identifier for backend reviews lookup
data_flows.provider_gate: Confirm email/support providers and logs. Current review lookup describes hotel data rather than guest booking details; external author-image/link requests can expose network metadata to Google. Re-audit if a native Maps SDK is selected.

observed_data: Existing web analytics helper dispatches local DOM events; this alone does not establish off-device analytics transmission

declaration_review_questions: Which flows actually run in the released native app, including account creation and membership?
What leaves the device, including SDKs and relevant server-to-server transfers?
For each actual data type, what purpose, required/optional status and deletion behavior apply?
Do any service-provider or user-initiated transfer exceptions apply? Do not blanket-declare no sharing.
Is all user data transmitted with appropriate transport protection across the complete app/SDK inventory?
Do the privacy notice, native disclosures, external deletion resource and actual backend retention agree?
